summary: Keep a state directory's node identity across computer renames and leave ordinary Claude sessions with an idle channel.

replay.detail: No claim replay or replicated history rewriting.

schema.detail: No database schema change. The daemon adds a private stable identity file and lifetime lock to its state directory.

rules.detail: No checkpoint or membership rule changes. Conflicting pinned fleet membership refuses startup.

compatibility.detail: Updated daemon, worker and service installer retain the same-state node identity instead of treating --node as a rename. Subject-less Claude MCP serves initialize, empty lists and ping without channel capability, tools or daemon access. Existing scoped channel admission remains intact.

downtime.detail: A daemon restart adopts the stable identity; running drivers can survive the outage. Specific macOS live-session recovery is unverified.

manual.detail: Back up before updating. For manually adopted seats or expired local launch receipts, restore the original launcher node before first updated startup; without proof that configured node becomes pinned and later --node changes cannot override it. Existing user-enabled st-channel may be disabled with claude plugin disable st-channel@st --scope user, then restart ordinary Claude. The updated installer keeps its assets installed but disables user activation; seat-local and per-process activation stays intact. Resolve ambiguous local history or conflicting fleet identity before startup.

recovery.detail: Keep original state, sockets, keys and stable identity. Revert launcher arguments to the recorded node for older binaries; older images ignore the new pin and lock. Do not restore a stale database, delete fleet state, edit member keys or bypass placement fences. Native-session preservation is tested with isolated runtime fixtures, not a live macOS provider.
